options.name: A — Refined Classic
options.prompt:
Use case: logo-brand.
Create a new, exceptionally well-crafted art-director's logo refinement sheet for HelloKahwin, a premium wedding editorial publication in Malaysia and Indonesia.
References: Image 1 is the previously approved wordmark comparison: ONLY THE FAR RIGHT "Fashion Publication" wordmark is the typography reference, with tall elegant fine-stem Didone letterforms and a straight restrained K. Image 2 is the six-symbol board: ONLY bottom-left "Editorial Seal", the HK inside a simple circle, is the mark reference. Ignore every other concept in the references.
Preserve the unified mixed-case name exactly "HelloKahwin" (H-e-l-l-o-K-a-h-w-i-n), same weight/color for whole word. The wordmark must have a straight, concise K leg. NO swash under the letters. No curl under "ahwin", no sweeping tails. The typography is airy, fine and quiet but dark enough to read. Small black-and-white color palette only.
Layout: one refined 4:3 landscape presentation sheet for ONE direction. Upper 70% white background with large seal, ample negative space, and an elegant unified HelloKahwin wordmark below. Bottom 30% solid black strip showing a smaller reversed white-on-black instance of EXACT SAME seal at left and EXACT SAME wordmark at right. Small title at upper left as specified. No invented copy, no sizes or performance claims.
Flat crisp vector-style appearance, clean white background with no paper texture, no shading, no gradients, no photographic mockups. Very simple geometrical border, optical centering, generous breathing room around glyphs; uniform competent drawing. No wedding rings, diamonds, hearts, wreaths, floral ornament, crowns, date or motto. These are alternatives within an editorial seal identity, not new wedding-symbol directions.
Title verbatim: "A / REFINED CLASSIC".
Design specification: Closest refinement of the chosen original. A perfect thin black circular outline, within which are interlocked high-contrast serif H and K. Two letters visibly legible, open internal spaces. Keep the gracious, mildly bowed H crossbar that joins into K but shorten the K terminal to an elegant straight diagonal ending, no sweeping swash. Fine bracketless serifs. Neither letter should swallow the other. Mark fills around 60% of inner circle width. Circular border at least as strong as the glyph hairline, not a double ring.

Mark should form ONE interlocked glyph rather than two fully drawn overlapping letters; no extra third vertical. Generous interior white space.
